correctness.rationale: For a chain, every tube is an interval and Sack's alpha_tau telescopes to an endpoint difference. The full-tube hyperplane fixes the total adjacent-gap sum. Projecting interval normals into the codimension-two tangent space gives norm sqrt(3/2) for endpoint intervals and sqrt(2) for internal intervals. Summing all two-element-facet ball inequalities yields the stated sharp upper bound. The proposed center realizes equality in every two-element facet. For a longer interval, the sum of adjacent normal lengths exceeds the interval normal by exactly (r-1)sqrt(2), and the explicit radius bound makes its excess slack strictly positive. Equality in the summed upper bound forces every adjacent gap and therefore the center uniquely.

value.rationale: Sack's realization is a recent explicit metric model of Galashin's poset associahedra, and the chain case is a canonical new realization of the classical associahedron rather than a mere relabeling of a Loday model. The theorem determines its exact inball in every dimension, explains the endpoint distortion caused by the codimension-two affine hull, and proves that the exponentially many larger-scale interval truncations are metrically inactive at the optimum. This is a natural realization-sensitive invariant of a central polytope family, not an arbitrary finite computation.
